entries.summary: Use non-blocking assignments (<=) inside clocked always blocks
entries.reasoning: 5 of the 18 train failures (Prob085_shift4, Prob118_history_shift, Prob063_review2015_shiftcount, ...) used blocking "=" inside always @(posedge clk). Every register in the chain then updates from the new value in the same cycle, so shift registers collapse to a single flop. One rule should fix the whole family.

entries.summary: Hold reset high for 3 cycles before releasing it
entries.reasoning: Two missed bugs involved designs that came out of reset in a bad state. Holding reset longer should expose them. Gate: only +1 on the frozen pool, below the +2 margin, so it is not worth the extra stimulus budget.

entries.summary: Ask the writer to restate every port and its width before coding
entries.reasoning: Three failures had port-width mismatches (Prob021_mux256to1v, Prob097_mux9to1v). Restating ports first might catch them. Gate: fixed 2 width bugs but the longer prompt broke 2 FSMs that had passed. Net 0, rejected.

entries.summary: New tool edge_sweep: toggle every control input right at clock edges
entries.reasoning: 7 of the 9 bugs we missed only showed up when reset or enable changed in the same cycle as a clock edge. Random stimulus almost never lines those up. A small generator that sweeps each control input across the edge should catch the whole class.

entries.summary: New tool lint_check: flag blocking assigns, SystemVerilog-only keywords and missing ports
entries.reasoning: Even with the round-1 rule, 4 drafts still slipped a blocking assign into a clocked block, and 2 used always_ff, which iverilog rejects. A static check before simulation lets the debugger fix these without burning an attempt.

entries.summary: Prefer continuous assign statements for purely combinational outputs
entries.reasoning: Combinational always blocks produced two latches. Pushing everything to assign should remove them. Gate: lost 2 mux problems where the assign got too long and the model mis-parenthesised it. Net -1, rejected.

entries.summary: Drive the widest bus with all-ones and all-zeros vectors first
entries.reasoning: Thought width bugs would show on the extremes. Gate: the pool bugs are mostly timing, not width; no change in catch rate. Rejected.

entries.summary: Put asynchronous resets in the sensitivity list: always @(posedge clk, posedge areset)
entries.reasoning: The Breaker's new edge_sweep tool exposed 4 designs that treated an "asynchronous" reset as synchronous. They pass most cycles, then hold a stale value for half a cycle whenever reset rises between edges. The spec wording "asynchronous" should map to the sensitivity list.

entries.summary: Walk every FSM state at least once, then force each illegal transition
entries.reasoning: Builder FSMs now pass basic sequences, so random inputs rarely reach the broken states. Reading the case statement, enumerating states and steering into each one found 3 bugs the pool had flagged but we had missed.

Six failures were one debug step away from compiling. A third attempt should rescue them. Gate: rescued 1, but the extra attempt rewrote a working counter into a broken one twice. Net -1, rejected, and it cost 30% more.

entries.summary: Read the design's case statements and aim inputs at the branches it is missing
entries.reasoning: The remaining misses are designs with incomplete case statements: they only fail on input values that hit a missing branch. Telling the attacker to list the covered cases and target the gaps is cheap and very specific.

entries.summary: Every case statement gets a default branch that assigns every output
entries.reasoning: The Breaker's new case-gap attacks caught 5 of our designs with incomplete case statements. Without a default, the output silently latches its previous value. Always assigning a default value removes the latch.

entries.summary: New tool x_probe: drive x and z values onto inputs to expose missing resets
entries.reasoning: Hoped unknown inputs would flush out designs that never initialise a register. Gate: x inputs propagate into the reference too, so 2 "bugs" were not reproducible and one real catch was lost. Net -1, rejected.
